```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette covers creating a yspec specification from a data frame, putting
its variables in data order, saving it, starting from the bundled NONMEM
specification, and using a specification to label plots.

```{r library}
library(yspecx)
```

## Create a specification from a data frame

`df_to_yspec()` writes a yspec YAML file from a data frame that describes the
variables.

```{r df-to-yspec}
variables <- data.frame(
  name = c("WEIGHT", "SEX", "AGE", "ID"),
  label = c("Body weight", "Sex", "Age", "Subject identifier"),
  unit = c("kg", NA, "years", NA),
  type = c("numeric", "character", "numeric", "numeric"),
  codes = c(NA, "F=Female, M=Male", NA, NA)
)

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
df_to_yspec(
  variables,
  desc = "Example data set",
  varname = "name",
  vardesc = "label",
  varunit = "unit",
  vartype = "type",
  varcodelist = "codes",
  output = path
)
spec <- yspec::ys_load(path)
names(spec)
```

Entries in the code list may be `code=label` or `label=code`, separated by
commas or new lines. Supply `codelist_func` to parse another format.

## Put variables in data order

`ys_sort_spec_vars()` orders the specification to match the columns of a data
frame. Specification variables that are not in the data follow, in their
original order, and data columns that are not in the specification are ignored.

```{r sort}
data <- data.frame(ID = 1, AGE = 35, SEX = "F", WEIGHT = 65)
sorted <- ys_sort_spec_vars(data, spec)
names(sorted)
```

## Save a specification

`ys_write()` writes a loaded or sorted specification back to YAML. The output
is a standalone specification: lookup results are written in full, derived
fields are omitted, and comments and formatting are not kept.

```{r write}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
ys_write(sorted, out)
names(yspec::ys_load(out))
```

## Start from the NONMEM specification

`ysx_load_pkpdspec()` loads a specification of standard NONMEM columns such as
`ID`, `TIME`, `DV`, `CMT`, `EVID` and `AMT`. Its `missing_code` is `-999`, `DV`
allows missing values, and `ID` is the group column.

```{r pkpd}
pkpd <- ysx_load_pkpdspec()
head(names(pkpd), 10)
pkpd$EVID$decode
```

## Label plots from a specification

`ysx_plt_relab()` relabels axis and legend titles and `facet_wrap()` or
`facet_grid()` strips from a specification, with units on axis titles. Coded
facet values are decoded.

```{r plot-data}
library(ggplot2)

dose <- data.frame(
  TIME = c(0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2),
  DV = c(0, 4, 3, 0, 5, 4),
  EVID = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
)
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
p <- ggplot(dose, aes(TIME, DV)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~EVID)

ysx_plt_relab(p, pkpd)
```

Use `label_type = "long"` or `"short"` to choose the specification field. An
error is raised if that field is missing for a plotted variable. Use `labs` for
custom labels, `facet_labels` for individual facet levels, and `var_map` when
the data name differs from the specification name.

```{r plot-options, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
renamed <- setNames(dose, c("time", "conc", "evid"))
p2 <- ggplot(renamed, aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~evid)

ysx_plt_relab(
  p2,
  pkpd,
  var_map = c(time = "TIME", conc = "DV", evid = "EVID"),
  label_type = "long",
  facet_labels = list(evid = c(`0` = "Observation", `1` = "Dose"))
)
```
